grading: Each expected_behavior line is pass/fail on the rewritten document alone. A grader who has not read the design doc must be able to decide each line. Anti-expectations are failures even if every expected line passes.
baseline_note: No-op lines were removed after the baseline pass; see evals/baselines/README.md. Do not re-add a line without checking the baseline fails it.

expected_behavior: Cites rule IDs for its changes (at least G-C1, G-W1, E-3) in the report, not only in the document.

Removes the restated npm commands and points at package.json instead of publishing its own copy of the script list (G-C1). Naming a script by its package.json name is fine; restating its flags and port is not.
Does not silently correct the drifted commands to match package.json and leave them cached — a fixed cache is still a cache.
Collapses ledger / transaction log / money record / journal to one term used everywhere (G-W1).

States that the term is a glossary candidate and that no glossary was found at docs/GLOSSARY.md or via an AGENTS.md pointer, and offers setup — without writing a glossary file (§4.1 never-as-a-side-effect).
Flags 'SDR checks' as an undefined coined term and either defines it at first use or asks (G-W2). Does not invent an expansion.
Restructures Getting started for lookup: prerequisites, install, run, test, migrate as separately addressable items rather than one narrative paragraph (E-3).
Gives each deploy step an observable check — what you should see if it worked (E-2). 'Check that the deploy worked' is not a check.
No sentence in the rewrite exceeds 25 words (G-S1).
Deletes the Notes section's no-op sentences (G-P1).
Reports any rule it chose not to apply as a waiver with a reason and a date (G-X1), or reports no waivers.
anti_expectations: Writes or edits docs/GLOSSARY.md, AGENTS.md, or any file other than the README.
Applies R1-S rules: inline stakeholder glosses, or a what-changed/why-it-matters section, in an engineer-facing README.
Strips stack terms (Node, npm, migration, bank feed) that R1-E permits (E-1).

scenarios.prompt: Rewrite this release note for customers.
expected_behavior: Classifies the document as R1-S and says so.
Reads the glossary named by the AGENTS.md pointer and uses Ledger and Settlement Window exactly, replacing journal / money record / batch window / nightly run (G-W1).
Glosses each glossary term inline at first use, using the gloss column rather than an improvised paraphrase (S-1).
Cuts or translates every stack term that reaches the reader: advisory lock, Postgres, cron, DLQ, consumer group, idempotency key, TTL, p99, covering index (S-1).
Orders the document what changed, why it matters to the reader, what happens next (S-2).
Reports the delay as problem, then impact on the customer, then next step — the lock-contention cause chain is cut or demoted below the impact (S-3).

Every number carries its comparison: latency stated against its previous value or its target, not as a bare 340ms (S-4). A number whose comparison is unavailable is removed or marked as needing the before value, not left bare.
Replaces 'customers who were affected may wish to reach out' with a concrete next step naming who acts and by when (S-2).
Drops the internal-only changes that do not change what the reader knows or does (G-P1).
No sentence in the rewrite exceeds 25 words (G-S1).
Cites rule IDs (at least S-1 through S-4) in the report.
anti_expectations: A competent engineer-facing rewrite passes this rubric — if the output keeps the cause chain, keeps stack terms because 'the audience is technical', or omits glosses, it fails regardless of prose quality.
Invents a before value for a number that the fixture does not supply.
Adds a glossary entry or edits the glossary file.

expected_behavior: Requirement 1 uses MUST for the absolute (G-N1).
Requirement 2's 'must probably' is resolved: either MUST with the condition stated, or SHOULD with the allowed exception stated — not both keywords in one clause (G-N1).
Requirement 4's 'it is intended that ... should' becomes one keyword with one meaning (G-N1).
Requirement 3 keeps only observable behavior; RefundService.apply, the advisory lock, the Drizzle client, and the two-row write move to a design section or are cut (E-4).
States the E-4 test when it moves something: the implementation can change without changing observable behavior.
Uses Ledger and Settlement Window from the glossary; transaction log, money record, journal, and cutoff are gone (G-W1).
Defines RRN at first use or flags it for the glossary (G-W2). Does not invent an expansion.
Rewrites each scenario as a sentence that can be read aloud: given, when, then — no arrow notation, no bare metric increments (spec prose is prose).
Deletes the Purpose section's no-op sentences (G-P1).
No sentence in the rewrite exceeds 25 words (G-S1).
Cites rule IDs (at least G-N1 and E-4) in the report.
anti_expectations: Imposes skeleton grammar: four-hashtag scenario headings, '- [ ] X.Y' requirement IDs, RFC-2119 delta keywords, or a linter-enforced structure. That machinery is deferred (design Appendix A); rewriting prose is in scope, regrammaring the artifact is not.
Rejects the document for not matching a spec template.
Translates the spec for non-technical readers (wrong register — spec prose is R1-E plus G-N1 and E-4).

scenarios.prompt: Set up a glossary for this repo.
expected_behavior: Asks where the glossary should live, or proposes docs/GLOSSARY.md, before writing anything.

Harvests the three planted synonym clusters: the Ledger cluster (ledger / transaction log / money record / journal), the Settlement Window cluster (batch window / cutoff / nightly run), and the Merchant cluster (merchant / seller / vendor / partner).
Harvests at least one recurring unnamed paraphrase — the repeated phrase for a payment that has been authorized but not yet captured — and proposes a term for it.
Presents candidates as a table with proposed term, draft meaning, detected synonyms, and draft stakeholder gloss.
Runs one batched round of closed accept/rename/trim questions rather than one question per entry.
Drafts a stakeholder gloss only for candidates that appear in a stakeholder-facing document, and says which document put them there.
Proposes no entry for API, webhook, or Postgres used in their ordinary industry sense (§4.1 stack-term admission).
Proposes 'Worker' as a narrowed-meaning entry, because the repo uses it for its own component rather than the generic sense.
Writes nothing to disk before the user approves, then writes only approved entries.
Writes the pointer line 'Glossary: <path>' to AGENTS.md.
Ends by stating the standing maintenance rule: propose, human approves, never as a side effect.
anti_expectations: Any file write before an explicit approval turn.
Writes every detected candidate, treating detections as decisions.
Hardcodes CONTEXT.md or CLAUDE.md as the glossary location instead of following the discovery chain.
